analysis.summary: Sedar produces high-quality initial seeds for DBMS fuzzing by transferring test cases from other DBMSs, addressing the problem that many systems lack comprehensive built-in test suites. The insight is that DBMSs share many features, so a seed reaching deep paths in one can be adapted for another. Sedar executes existing test cases in their original DBMS while capturing schema information, uses an LLM guided by that information to generate new cases, and comments out unparsable sections so fuzzers can mutate them. It found 70 new vulnerabilities.
analysis.narrative: Three citations in related work describing SQLancer's oracles -- NoREC, PQS and query plan guidance -- as the generation-based approaches aimed at specific bug types, in contrast to Sedar's coverage-guided seed transfer.
